semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ}: there are several possibilities. The first is that it is an address to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the plural form, as a mark of honour, as in his saying:
4271 - فإنْ شِئْتِ حَرَّمْتُ النساءَ سواكمُ ... وإن شِئْتِ لم أَطْعَمْ نُقاخاً ولا بَرْدا
(If you wish, I will forbid women other than you; and if you wish, I will not taste cool sweet water, nor sleep.)
The second is that it is an address to him and to his community, the implied form being: "O Prophet, and your community, when you divorce", with the conjoined element omitted because what comes after indicates it, as in his saying:
4272 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... إذا حَذْفَتْه رِجْلُها. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(... when her foot flung it...)
that is, "and her hand"; and this was given in Sūrat al-Naḥl at {تَقِيكُمُ الحر} [al-Naḥl: 81]. The third is that it is an address to his community only, after calling him, peace be upon him, and this is a variation of address (talwīn al-khiṭāb): He addressed his community after He had addressed him. The fourth is that it is on the basis of an implied "say", that is: "O Prophet, say to your community: when you divorce." The fifth: al-Zamakhsharī said: "He singled out the Prophet ﷺ for the vocative and generalized in the address, because the Prophet is the leader of his community and their model, as one says to the chief of a people and their elder: 'O so-and-so, do such-and-such,' having regard to his precedence and showing his headship," in fine words; and this is the meaning of the third view, which I gave earlier.
And His saying {إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ} means: "when you intend", like His saying {إِذَا قُمْتُمْ إِلَى الصلاة} [al-Māʾida: 6] and {فَإِذَا قَرَأْتَ القرآن} [al-Naḥl: 98]; and the verification of that has been given.
His saying: {لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "facing their ʿidda (waiting period), as you say «أتيتُه لِلَيْلَةٍ بَقِيَتْ من المحرَّم», that is, 'facing it'; and in the reading of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: «في قُبُل عِدَّتِهِنَّ»." End. The Shaykh took issue with him over his implying, for the ḥāl to which the preposition is attached, a specific being (kawn khāṣṣ), and said: "When a preposition and its genitive noun occurs as a ḥāl, it is attached only to an unspecified being." In his objection there is room for doubt, because al-Zamakhsharī did not make the preposition and its genitive noun a ḥāl, but made it attached to an omitted element which the meaning of the speech indicates. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ», that is, at the first moment at which they are counted for them, while they are at the beginning of the period of purity (qubul al-ṭuhr)." This is, on his part, an explanation of meaning and not an explanation of i'rāb. The Shaykh said: "It is on an omitted muḍāf, that is, «لاستقبالِ عِدَّتِهِن», and the lām is for fixing a time, like «لَقِيْتُه لِلَيْلَةٍ بَقِيَتْ مِنْ شهرِ كذا»." End. On this the lām is attached to «طَلِّقُوهن».
His saying: {لَعَلَّ الله}: this clause is resumptive, with no connection between it and what precedes, because the grammarians did not count it among the suspending particles (muʿallaqāt). The Shaykh held it to be among those that ought to be counted among them, and established that in His saying {وَإِنْ أَدْرِي لَعَلَّهُ فِتْنَةٌ لَّكُمْ} [al-Anbiyāʾ: 111]; its treatment is to be sought there.

semin-durr:2-2.t: The majority read {أَجَلَهُنَّ}, because the term, as such, is one, even if its kinds differ in relation to the women observing a waiting period. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Ibn Sīrīn read «آجالَهُنَّ», a broken plural, taking into account that the term of this one is other than the term of that one.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {بَالِغُ أَمْرِهِ}: Ḥafṣ read «بالغُ» without tanwīn, «أمرِه» being the muḍāf ilayhi, for lightness. The others read it with tanwīn and the accusative, which is the original, contrary to the Shaykh. Ibn Abī ʿAbla, Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind, and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission, read «بالغٌ أمرُه» with tanwīn on «بالغٌ» and «أَمْرُه» nominative, and there are two possibilities in it. The first is that «بالغٌ» is a fronted khabar and «أمْرُه» a postponed mubtadaʾ, the clause being the khabar of «إنَّ». The second is that «بالغٌ» is the khabar of «إنَّ» and «أَمْرُه» is its agent. Al-Mufaḍḍal read «بالغاً» in the accusative and «أَمْرُه» in the nominative. There are two possibilities in it, the clearer of which, al-Zamakhsharī's explanation, is that «بالغاً» is accusative as a ḥāl, and {قَدْ جَعَلَ الله} is the khabar of «إنَّ», its implied form being: "Allah has set for everything a measure, its command reaching [its end]." The second is that it is on the dialect of those who put both the noun and the khabar of it in the accusative, as in his saying:
4273 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . إنَّ حُرَّاسَنا أُسْدا
(... indeed our guards are lions.)
and «قد جَعَل» is resumptive, as in the well-known reading. As for the one who put «أَمْرُه» in the nominative, the object of «بالغ» is omitted, its implied form being: "what He wills". Jināḥ ibn Ḥubaysh read «قَدَرا» with fatḥa on the dāl.

semin-durr:4-4.t:
His saying: {واللائي يَئِسْنَ}: the disagreement about it has already been given. Abū ʿAmr reads here «واللايْ يَئِسْنَ» with clear pronunciation (iẓhār), whereas his rule in the like of it is assimilation (idghām); except that, since the yāʾ in his view is incidental, being a substitute for a hamza, it is as though two like letters had not met. Moreover its quiescence is incidental, so it is as though the yāʾ of «اللاي» were vowelled, and a letter, as long as it is vowelled, is not assimilated into another. He read «يَئِسْنَ» as a past verb; «يَيْئَسْنَ» was also read, as an imperfect. And «مِنْ المحيض مِنْ نسائكم»: the first «مِنْ» is for the beginning of the extent (ibtidāʾ al-ghāya), attached to the verb before it, and the second is for clarification, attached to an omitted element. «اللائي» is a mubtadaʾ, «فعِدَّتُهُنَّ» is a second mubtadaʾ, «وثلاثةُ أشهر» is its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of the first; the condition is parenthetical, and its apodosis is omitted. It is also possible that «إنِ ارْتَبْتُم» has as its apodosis {فَعِدَّتُهُنَّ ثَلاَثَةُ أَشْهُرٍ}, the conditional clause being the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. What the doubt is attached to is omitted; it was said that its implied form is: "if you doubt whether she has reached the age of despair or not, owing to the possibility of a pregnancy appearing, even though her blood has stopped." It was also said: "if you doubt about the blood of those who have reached the age of despair, whether it is menstrual blood or irregular bleeding." And if this is the waiting period of those about whom there is doubt, then those about whom there is no doubt are more deserving of it. The most strange of what was said is that «إنْ ارتَبْتُم» is in the sense of "if you are certain", so it would be one of the words with opposite meanings (aḍdād).
His saying: {واللائي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ}: a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted. They implied a clause like the first, that is: "their waiting period is also three months"; the better is to imply a single word, that is: "likewise", or "like them". And if it were said that it is conjoined to «اللائي يَئِسْنَ» as a conjunction of single words, and the khabar given for all of them by His saying «فعِدَّتُهنَّ», that would be a fine view; the most that can be said against it is the placing of the khabar between the mubtadaʾ and what is conjoined to it. This is the apparent meaning of the Shaykh's saying: {واللائي لَمْ يَحِضْنَ} is conjoined to «واللائي يَئِسْن», so its i'rāb as a mubtadaʾ is like the i'rāb of «واللائي».
His saying: {وَأُوْلاَتُ الأحمال}: a mubtadaʾ, and «أَجَلُهُنَّ» a second mubtadaʾ, and «أن يَضَعْن» its khabar, the clause being the khabar of the first, that is, "the delivery of their burden". It is also possible that «أَجلُهنَّ» is a badal ishtimāl (inclusion substitute) from «أُولات», and «أنْ يضعن» the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. The majority read «حَمْلهنَّ» in the singular; al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «آجالُهُنَّ», a broken plural.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {وَيُعْظِمْ}: this is the reading of the majority, the imperfect of أَعْظَمَ; Ibn Miqsam read «يُعَظِّمْ» with shadda, the imperfect of عَظَّم with shadda. Al-Aʿmash read «نُعْظِم», the imperfect of أَعْظم, which is an iltifāt (shift of person) from the third person to the first.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {مِنْ حَيْثُ سَكَنتُم}: there are two possibilities. The first is that «مِنْ» is partitive. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "What is partitioned is omitted; its meaning is: house them in a place from where you dwell, that is, part of the place of your dwelling, as in the saying of the Exalted: {يَغُضُّواْ مِنْ أَبْصَارِهِمْ} [al-Nūr: 30], that is, part of their sight. Qatāda said: 'If there is only one house, let him house her in part of its sides.'" The second is that it is for the beginning of the extent, as al-Ḥawfī and Abū l-Baqāʾ said. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The meaning: take steps to house them in the way in which you house yourselves. His saying «مِنْ وُجْدِكم» indicates this, الوُجْد being wealth."
His saying: {مِّن وُجْدِكُمْ}: there are two possibilities. The first is that it is a badal from His saying «مِنْ حيثُ» with repetition of the governor, and Abū l-Baqāʾ held this, as if it were said: "house them from your means." The second is that it is an ʿaṭf bayān of His saying {مِنْ حَيْثُ سَكَنتُم}, and al-Zamakhsharī held this, for he said, after parsing «مِنْ حيث» as partitive as above: "If you ask: and what of His saying «مِنْ وُجْدِكم»? I say: it is an ʿaṭf bayān of His saying {مِنْ حَيْثُ سَكَنتُم} and an explanation of it, as if it were said: house them in a place among your dwellings, of what you can afford. الوُجْد is capacity and ability." The Shaykh took issue with him, saying that repetition of the governor is not known in ʿaṭf bayān; it is known only in the badal, and for that reason Abū l-Baqāʾ parsed it as a badal. The majority read «وُجْدِكم» with ḍamma on the wāw; al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj and Abū Ḥaywa with fatḥa; al-Fayyāḍ ibn Ghazwān, ʿAmr ibn Maymūn and Yaʿqūb with kasra, which are dialects of one meaning. And الوَجْد with fatḥa on the wāw is also grief, love and anger.
His saying: {وَأْتَمِرُواْ}: ifʿalū from الأَمْر. One says: ايتَمَرَ القومُ and تآمروا, that is, they commanded one another. Al-Kisāʾī said: ائتمروا means "they consulted one another", and he recited the saying of the Exalted {إِنَّ الملأ يَأْتَمِرُونَ بِكَ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 20], and recited the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:
4274 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ويَعْدُوْ على المَرْءِ ما يَأَتْمِرْ
(... and what a man plans turns upon him.)
His saying: {فَسَتُرْضِعُ}: it was said: it is a khabar in the sense of a command. The pronoun in «له» refers to the father, as in His saying {فَإِنْ أَرْضَعْنَ لَكُمْ}, and the object is omitted because it is known, that is: "another woman will nurse the child for his father." The apparent sense is that it is a khabar in its ordinary sense.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {لِيُنفِقْ}: this is the reading of the majority, I mean kasra on the lām and jussive of the imperfect by it. Abū Muʿādh the reader reported «لِيُنْفِقَ» with the verb in the accusative, the lām being the lām of purpose (lām kay), the verb after it put in the accusative by an implied «أَنْ», and the preposition is then attached to an omitted element, that is: "We legislated that so that he may spend." The majority read «قُدِر» lightened; Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «قَدَّر» with shadda.

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {عَتَتْ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهَا}: it was made to imply the sense of "turned away", as if it were said: "it turned away because of its insolence." And His saying «فحاسَبْناها» to the end is all in the Hereafter, and He put it in the past wording because of its certainty. It was also said: the punishment is in this world, in which case it is taken in its literal sense. And «أعدَّ الله» is a repetition of the threat and an emphasis. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed that «عَتَتْ» and what is conjoined to it be a ṣifa of «قريةٍ», and that the khabar of «كأيِّنْ» be the clause from His saying «أعدَّ اللَّهُ»; whereas on the first view the khabar is «عَتَتْ» and what is conjoined to it.

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {الذين آمَنُواْ}: accusative by an implied «أَعْني» ("I mean"), as a clarification of the one addressed; or it is an ʿaṭf bayān for the one addressed, or a naʿt of it; and its being a badal is weak, because it cannot take the place of that for which it is a substitute.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His saying: {رَّسُولاً}: there are several possibilities. The first, which al-Zajjāj and al-Fārisī held, is that it is accusative by the maṣdar with tanwīn before it, because that dissolves into a maṣdar-particle and a verb, as if it were said: "that He mentioned a messenger"; and a maṣdar with tanwīn governs, as in the saying of the Exalted {أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيماً} [al-Balad: 14] and in his saying: 4275 - بضَرْبٍ بالسيوفِ رؤوسَ قَوْمٍ ... أَزَلْنا هامَهُنَّ عن المَقيلِ
(By striking with swords the heads of a people, we removed their skulls from their resting place.)
The second is that the remembrance itself was made [the messenger] by way of exaggeration, and so a badal was made from it. The third is that it is a badal from it with an omitted muḍāf from the first, the implied form being: "He sent down one possessing a reminder, a messenger." The fourth is likewise, except that «رسولاً» is a naʿt of that omitted element. The fifth is that it is a badal from it with an omitted muḍāf from the second, that is: "a reminder, the reminder of a messenger." The sixth is that «رسولاً» is a naʿt of «ذِكْراً» with an omitted muḍāf, that is: "a reminder possessing a messenger", so «ذا رسول» is a naʿt of «ذِكْر». The seventh is that «رسولاً» is in the sense of "message" (risāla), so that «رسولاً» is an outright badal without interpretation, or a clarification according to those who allow it in indefinites, such as al-Fārisī; but his saying «يَتْلُو عليكم» makes this remote, because a message does not recite except figuratively. The eighth is that «رسولاً» is accusative by an implied verb, that is: "He sent a messenger", as what precedes indicates it. The ninth is that it is accusative as incitement (ighrāʾ), that is: "follow, and hold fast to, a messenger of this description."
The people differed about «رسولاً»: is he the Prophet ﷺ, or the Qur'ān itself, or Jibrīl? Al-Zamakhsharī said: "He is Jibrīl, peace be upon him," made a badal from «ذِكْراً» because he is described as reciting the verses of Allah, so that his sending down is in the sense of sending down the Reminder, and therefore making him a badal from it is sound. The Shaykh said: "It is not sound, because of the difference in the referents in reality, and because it is neither a badal of part nor a badal of inclusion." End. What al-Zamakhsharī said was preceded in it by al-Kalbī. As for his objection to it, it is not necessarily so, because it is by exaggeration, until he was made the very Reminder, as its explanation was given earlier. «رسولٌ» was also read, with an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: "he is a messenger."
His saying: {لِّيُخْرِجَ}: attached either to «أَنْزَل» or to «يَتْلو». The agent of «يُخْرِج» is either the pronoun of the Creator, the Exalted, who sends down, or the pronoun of the Messenger, or of the Reminder. And «مَنْ يُؤْمِنْ» is one of the places where the wording was regarded first, then the meaning second, then the wording last, as was given in [Sūrat] al-Māʾida. Some interpreted this verse [and said: His saying «خالدين» has no pronoun in it returning to «مَنْ»; it returns only to the object of «يُدْخِلْه», and «خالدين» is a ḥāl from it, and the governor in it is «يُدْخِلْه», not the verb of the condition]. This is the Shaykh's expression, and there is room for objection in it, because «خالدين» is a ḥāl from the object of «يُدْخِلْه» in the view of those who hold the first view; and the correction of the expression would be to say: a ḥāl from the second object of «يُدْخِلْه», which is «جناتٍ», and the abiding is in reality for their inhabitants; and in the view of the Basrans it should have been said «خالدين هم فيها», because the description is applied to other than the one to whom it belongs.
His saying: {قَدْ أَحْسَنَ الله}: a second ḥāl, or a ḥāl from the pronoun in «خالدين», in which case it is nested.

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {مِثْلَهُنَّ}: the majority read it in the accusative, and there are two possibilities. The first is that it is conjoined (ʿaṭf) to «سَبْعَ سماواتٍ»; al-Zamakhsharī said this. The Shaykh objected, because it requires separation, by a preposition and its genitive noun, between the conjunction, which is a single letter, and the conjoined, and this is restricted to poetic necessity in the view of Abū ʿAlī. I say: this is parallel to His saying {آتِنَا فِي الدنيا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الآخرة حَسَنَةً} [al-Baqara: 201] in the view of Ibn Mālik, and the treatment of this disagreement has been given in [Sūrat] al-Baqara, al-Nisāʾ and Hūd, at His saying {وَإِذَا حَكَمْتُمْ بَيْنَ الناس} [al-Nisāʾ: 58] and {وَمِن وَرَآءِ إِسْحَاقَ يَعْقُوبَ} [Hūd: 71].
The second is that it is accusative by an implied element after the wāw, that is: "and He created the like of them from the earth." The people differed about the likeness: it was said: like them in number. It was also said: in some attributes, since likeness is true by that; and the first is the well-known one. ʿĀṣim in one transmission read «مثلُهُنَّ» in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ, with the preposition and its genitive noun before it as its khabar.
His saying {يَتَنَزَّلُ}: it may be resumptive, and it may be a naʿt of what precedes; Abū l-Baqāʾ said this. Abū ʿAmr in one transmission, and ʿĪsā, read «يُنَزِّل» with shadda, that is, Allah; «الأمر» is the direct object. The pronoun in «بينهنَّ» refers to the heavens and the earths in the view of the majority, or to the heavens and the earth in the view of those who say that it is a single earth.
His saying: {لتعلموا}: attached to «خَلَقَ» or to «يَتنزَّل». The majority read «لتعلَموا» in the second person, and some with a yāʾ of the third person.
